name: Identifiable
first: A protocol for a type whose values each have an identity, a value that stays the same while their other properties change.

dependsOn.why: Identifiable is a protocol, whose one requirement is a property that gives each value its identity.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The type `Trip` conforms to `Identifiable` by having `id`, as `Friendly` conforms to `Greeter` by having `greet(name:)`.

dependsOn.why: An identifiable type is often a structure, whose instances are copied, so an identity is what says that two copies are the same item.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The type `Trip` is a structure, as `Trip` is on the page of Structure, so `trips[0]` holds its own copy of each value.

what.is: A type that conforms to the protocol `Identifiable` has a property named `id`, which gives each value its identity. The identity stays the same while the value's other properties change, so code can tell which item a value is after it changes or moves.
what.afterExample: Line 11 changes the city of the first trip, and line 12 moves it to the end of the array. Its `id` is still 1, so lines 13 to 17 find it again, and print its new city.
what.problem: A structure is copied, so two copies of a trip are two separate values, and after a trip's city changes, nothing in its values says it is the same trip as before. An identity that never changes says which item a value is, so code, and SwiftUI, can follow one item through every change.
what.how: The protocol requires one property, `id`, whose type must be hashable, such as `Int` or `String`. Apple's documentation says that the `id` identifies an item even when its other data changes. Code compares two items' `id` to tell whether they are the same item.

when.text: Use it for the items of a list that changes, such as trips that the user edits, adds, and deletes, so that each one can be followed by its `id`.
Don't make `id` a value that can change, such as `city`. A changed id would make the same item look like a new one.

parts.name: The conformance to `Identifiable`, line 1
parts.text: The colon and the name `Identifiable` after `Trip` say that `Trip` conforms to the protocol `Identifiable`. Its one requirement is a property named `id`.

parts.name: The property `id`, line 2
parts.text: Each trip has an `id`, of type `Int`. It is a constant, declared with `let`, so no code can change it, while `city` is a variable that code can change.

steps.text: Lines 6 to 9 make an array of two trips, whose ids are 1 and 2.
Line 10 keeps the id of the first trip in `chosen`.
Line 11 changes the city of that trip to `"Cusco"`. Its `id` is still 1.
Line 12 reverses the array, so that trip is now the second one.
Lines 13 to 17 go through the trips and find the one whose `id` is `chosen`. Line 15 prints its city: {{Cusco}}.

end.text: The trip moved and its city changed, but its `id` stayed 1, so the code found the same trip by its `id`.
